Class PartContainer

StateBehaviorContext
public abstract class PartContainer extends SysMLPart
A Part that executes in a separate process.

Part as process

PartContainer is a SysMLinJava implementation of a software container for executing SysMLParts in separate operating system processes. The PartContainer permits execution of models with virtually unlimited scale and performance as the model can be distributed across as many computers and CPUs and as much memory as is available. The PartContainer is, itself, a type of SysMLPart in that it contains "parts" and the connectors between these parts just as the typical SysMLPart does. However, in order to interact with and between other parts that execute in other PartContainers in other processes and/or other computers, the PartContainer also has "replicas" of the external parts with which its internal parts must be connected to as well. The ExternalPartReplica is simply an instantiation of the external part type in the context of the PartContainer. This replica instantiation is not actually executed. It is used solely to connect internal parts to the external part replica. Specifically, the container's internal parts' ports are connected to the external part's ports via the IP address and UDP port values of the replica parts. The ports of these internal parts recognize the connected port as external to the container and therefore utilize the IP address/UDP port values to communicate with the external part's port via the UDP protocol instead of via direct receive(signal) operation invocation as is the case when the port is in the same operating system process.

Inter-process Part connectors

Because some of the ports in the PartContainer's parts communicate with ports in other PartContainers' parts (via the UDP/IP protocol), it is important that these ports be constructed/initialized in their context Part with an assigned IP address and UDP port. The SysMLFullPort has a single constructor dedicated to this type of instantiation. Any port in any part in the container that is to receive signals from ports in parts in other containers, i.e. between OS processes, must be constructed this way in the part's createFullPorts() operation.

Connecting parts in different Part containers

Creation/instantiation of the external part replicas should be performed within the createExternalPartReplicas() operation. Connecting the internal parts to the external parts represented by the replicas should be performed within the createExternalConnectorFunctions() and createExternalConnectors() operations. Connection is performed just as it is for connecting ports in parts in the same process/container/Part, i.e. via the SysMLPort's addConnectedPeer(SysMLPort) operation.

Example

An example of how to create a model in a specialized/extended class of the PartContainer follows. Examples of how to create the elements in an extension/specialization of the PartContainer are provided in the comment blocks for the operations declared below. The examples are based on this example declaration of container parts and connectors. 
@Part
public YankeePart yankee;
@Part
public ZuluPart zulu;

@ExternalPartReplica
public AlphaPart alpha;
@ExternalPartReplica
public BravoPart bravo;

@AssociationConnectorFunction
public SysMLAssociationPartConnectorFunction connectorFunction;

@AssociationConnector
public SysMLAssociationPartConnector connector;

@ExternalAssociationConnectorFunction
public SysMLExternalAssociationPartConnectorFunction externalConnectorFunction;

@ExternalAssociationConnector
public SysMLExternalAssociationPartConnector externalConnector;

@Override
protected void createParts()
{
        yankee = new Yankee();
        zulu = new Zulu();
}

@Override
protected void createExternalPartReplicas()
{
        alpha = new AlphaPart();
        bravo = new BravoPart();
}

@Override
protected void createExternalConnectorFunctions()
{
        externalConnectorFunctionYankeeToAlpha = () -> yankee.outPort.addConnectedPortPeer(alpha.inPort);
        externalConnectorFunctionZuluToBravo = () -> zulu.outPort.addConnectedPortPeer(bravo.inPort);
}

@Override
protected void createExternalConnectors()
{
        externalConnectorYankeeToAlpha = new SysMLExternalAssociationPartConnector(yankee, alpha, externalConnectorFunctionYankeeToAlpha);
        externalConnectorZuluToBravo = new SysMLExternalAssociationPartConnector(zulu, bravo, externalConnectorFunctionZuluToBravo);
}

  • Method Details

    • createParts

      protected void createParts()
      Overridable operation to create the containers parts and external part replicas used to create the connectors between parts in this container and external parts in other containers. An example of how to create the external part replicas is as follows: 
      alphaPart = new AlphaPart();
bravoPart = new BravoPart();
      As described above, the part "replica" instances are just replicas of the part instances that are located in other PartContainers running in other processes on the same or different computers or CPUs. The replicas are instantiated solely to provide a local context in which the Part container can be compiled with all of its parts. Designation of the part of a replica is used to form the connectors with the actual part located in another Part container in another process, possibly in another computer.
      Overrides:
      createParts in class SysMLItem
      See Also:
      • SysMLPart

    • createFlowConnectors

      protected void createFlowConnectors()
      Overridable operation to create the connectors between parts that are internal to this container and parts that are external in other containers. The creation of the connectors is essentially the same as it is between parts internal to the connector, i.e. creating the SysMLExternalAssociationPartConnector with the SysMLExternalAssociationPartConnectorFunction as an initializing argument. The difference is the connectors connecting function uses the "replica" parts for those parts that are located in another Part container, i.e. in another process. An example of how to create the connector is as follows: 
      externalConnector = new SysMLExternalAssociationPartConnector(List.of(yankeePart, zuluPart), List.of(alphaPart, bravoPart), externalConnectorFunction);
      Overrides:
      createFlowConnectors in class SysMLPart
      See Also:
      • SysMLFlowConnector
